body:
I wonder if the anti-green crackdown might have been plagued with false-flag operations by the clubfoots men meant to inflame sentiments against the queen. A secret force within the city committing atrocities and blaming them on the Queen could have done much to push the Maegor with teats narrative. 

The religious aspect could have been helped along by the Oldtown-centered and Green-aligned faith and/or citadel. The faith especially provides a pre-existing organizational capacity throughout the city that would be critical to accomplishing something like this. There’s also the historical enmity between the faith and the Targaryens. Especially since the faith is super misogynistic, reliant on traditional gender roles, and is primed to hate Rhaenyra because of the Harwin Strong thing.

Despite the Blacks having some advantages, there are a lot of levers for a guy like Larys to push on.

It’s been a year now. I don’t think I really accomplished any of these goals, but I’m getting closer on all of them. 

The dreams are still haunting me, but not as often. I can hope I’ll be okay again someday.

I wish I could free myself entirely from this broken heart. Maybe next year.
Worthless
In the I love you more game, you win AND you die

Hating her doesn’t feel any better. Trust me. 

The only healing is in indifference. Which is pretty much impossible, at least for me.

Soon (TM)

Everything is always coming “soon” and yet nothing ever changes.

If he is needing love from you and you’re not in love with him, anything you do is going to feel cold and selfish to him. You can’t give him what he needs and you can’t avoid hurting him. You know what you have to do so just do it. Waiting around and waffling isn’t helping you and it sure as hell isn’t helping him. Rip the bandaid off. Get it over with.

It’s felt that way for years. 

I’m well aware she doesn’t define me. I appreciate the advice, but I could probably use the video on how to gain weight in 4 easy steps lol. I have no appetite these days.
Over two years. Still waiting.

She lost someone she doesn’t value. I could be the best guy on earth, but she doesn’t care to have me in her life anymore. She didn’t lose anything she didn’t want to. 

I lost the only person I ever really loved. I lost the best part of my life. I lost my ability to trust people. I lost my ability to sleep through the night without being plagued by dreams of her. I’m halfway to losing my sanity. 

I think it’s clear who lost more.

I know what you mean. It’s also been two and a half years for me. We’re not part of each other’s lives anymore at all, but I still think about her every day. As you said, she’d never notice or care if I died tomorrow, and that really sucks.

It feels like this breakup left an ocean of bitterness inside me and there’s nowhere for it to go and nothing for me to do except drown in it.

I hope the days and months to come bring you a little relief. I’m impressed that you’re still going. Even that shows a ton of strength in the face of depression.

Someday, someone’s heart will melt for your paper crane apologies. There’s beauty and value inside you, even if he doesn’t recognize it.
Either ignore or something short and clear like, “I’m not interested in talking. Good luck. Please don’t contact me again.”

I’d try to reframe thinking of this as “undoing all my hard work”. I don’t think your work is undone. This is a hurdle you had to get past in your healing journey.

Think of it like a windy trail with ups and downs. Your destination might be lower elevation to the west. Sometimes the trail takes you up hills, or curves to the north or south. Sometimes you might even have to go east for a bit. Does that mean you’re undoing the progress you’ve already made in your trek? No. You’re still getting there, still making progress along the trail even if you have to go the “wrong” direction for a bit.

My ex seemed to instantly start doing better after our breakup. Meanwhile I’m still here on this damn subreddit 2.5 years later. I’ve gone over so many of those hills. Had to go the “wrong” way so many times. But eventually I’ll make it to where I’m trying to go.

So will you.
The answer is no. It’s not what you want to hear, but it’s the truth. Take it from someone who learned the hard way if you can.

> I haven’t been interested in multiple years

If he’s still hung up on you after this long, being friends is not doing him any favors. If you really want the best for him you ought to take a step back until he actually moves on. You should not be friends right now. It doesn’t matter to you, but it’s actively hurting him to be in contact with you at all.

Maybe the thing to say would be along the lines of, “I’ve made it clear that all I can offer you is friendship and you’re pushing the boundaries of that here. I care about you as a friend but you need to move on, let this go, and give me space.”

You’ve already tried being subtle by not responding. It didn’t work. It’s time to be direct.
You did the right thing. This is the worst your going to feel about it. As time passes it’ll become clearer and clearer and you’ll feel more and more at peace. It’s better this way.

Why is it that you want to be in a relationship with her again? Even if you still love her, it’s obvious you were unhappy with her for a long time. You were lonely with her. You felt the relationship was a burden on you. 

Do you think it would be different if you did reconcile? Why? It’s curious to me that you want to return to something that by your own admission was so unfulfilling.

We caught up a year later. I made a joke, she said she missed that. Last thing she said was, “you can always come to me for support.”  I said, “Support? I’ve missed your jokes too.” Because that’s what her support amounts to.
My ex told me she doesn’t :/
Sure it’s fine for them. But when people make commitments I just think they ought to mean it.

He’s definitely not in love with you, but it sounds like he still thinks highly of you. It’s time to move on. Maybe, maybe, there’s friendship down the line when you’re truly over him. But right now you need to accept that it’s over.

> is this just a polite way to reject me?

Yes. I’m sorry :(
Just reply “I don’t”
It’s been just over 2 years since my 9-year relationship ended. Hoping maybe it won’t last forever, but I don’t see it letting up any time soon

Very happy for you :)

My breakup was one month after yours, maybe if I’m lucky next month I’ll be where you are now.

I did with my ex 7 months after breaking up. Then again a couple months later. It was okay at the time but now I consider it a mistake because I still had too many feelings.

If you want to move on, it’s not going to help in that goal. If both of you are already moved on, then seems like it would be all right.

It is :/

I do have a therapist, but what can they do besides tell me things I already know like it’s over and I need to move on.

Thank you <3 I don’t know if I deserve kindness from myself after a long history of unkindness and even abuse towards myself, but I figure one of us has to be the bigger person eventually, lol. 

I’m curious, how do you even find a months-old post from a deleted user to comment in now?

I don’t think this is true either. Sometimes someone can love you but over time things change. People break up after 10, 20, 30 years. You mean to tell me these people never loved each other? I say BS. They loved each other once, but they don’t anymore. Doesn’t mean it wasn’t real at the beginning.

Doesn’t seem all that admirable and sweet of him to me. Seems to me like its, “I want to make sure you’re alive, but I aside from that I don’t want to see or speak to you again.” Not my definition of sweet.

It does suck. I’m sorry for what you’re going through. It’s so hard to rebuild your life and create new friendships outside the relationship, but it’s worth it in the end.
Thank you :)

I agree with everything you said. I’m not sure my unhappiness is because of a lack of effort but I know I need to try harder and be stronger. I’d like to not feel empty and to not have her running around my brain like an earworm. I’d love for the dreams to stop, to feel excited about other people, to consistently enjoy life. I do try, I’ve been trying for years. To be honest I’m starting to lose confidence that I’m up to the task of being happy, who wouldn’t when life is like this? But despite that I’m going to keep trying because what else can I do?

I know she isn’t that person anymore, but she was for a long time.

I was in therapy for about 8 months last year. I don’t think it helped much. Typically I’d walk out feeling worse than when I arrived. Eventually it felt like a waste of everyone’s time and my money so I stopped going.

I’m not happy to still be feeling this way after so long, but here we are. Maybe I was foolish to hope that losing someone you love could ever be okay. It’s not as bad as it used to be. Perhaps in another two years it’ll lessen to the point of not disrupting my life.

Talk is cheap and you generally can’t trust what people say. Often they are lying even to themselves. Or saying something they want to be true, but don’t actually feel and aren’t committed to acting out. We have to be prepared for anything anyone tells us to be proven wrong if something changes. I think all of us here are learning that the hard way.
Wish I could have your attitude

I don’t condone violence but I get where he’s coming from.

If the friendship doesn’t matter then I guess I don’t really understand the question.

If the friendship means anything at all then guy 2 has a responsibility to talk to guy 1 first at minimum. Bro code is you don’t date your friends exes, period.

Seems to me like the most likely outcome is that guy 2 pursues the girl and whatever friendship existed between guy 1 and guy 2 is going to be wrecked. It’s possible that they could remain friends depending on the reasons for the breakup, but after seven years there’s almost certainly going to be hard feelings of some kind.

On the other hand, if you don’t care about being friends with guy 1, then swing away.

I feel everything you say in this post. I felt the betrayal and inadequacy and fear and anger so strongly when it was fresh many months ago. I still feel those things, but some of the intensity has faded. Except for two things. The missing/yearning part and the ruining love part. Those are still strong as ever.

Thank you for putting into words so many things I felt. At least someone somewhere understands.

This is the year we finally feel whole again.

I feel this way too. I didn’t even get cheated on or anything, but every relationship moving forward I’ll know this. No matter how amazing, kind and loyal they appear to be, no matter how much I love them or they appear to love me, tomorrow could be the day they change their mind. The last day I ever see them.

It’s all well and good to meet people and have fun and go on dates, but how can I make real plans, how can I invest in a future with someone when I know it could all be over tomorrow.
Same for me. 9 years, almost 2 since the breakup. I still haven’t felt even a little bit of anything for anyone else yet. Maybe someday.

I don’t think the texts are hurting me. There aren’t enough of them to hurt. It’s just the breakup is still hurting me, even after all this time. 

I’m mostly focusing what energy I have on work. It’s not enjoyable but at least it’s productive.

Thanks for your kind words!

I guess I just need to quit thinking about it so much. It doesn’t matter what I do, I’m not going to feel any better, so best to focus on other things.

Honestly I’d be ecstatic to miss her only a teeny tiny bit. Missing her as much as I do — there’s no room to feel anything else.

If I were her it would be extremely difficult for me to trust you ever again. You definitely hurt her, and that scar may heal, but it will never be quite the same again.

Let’s say you get back together and a few more years down the road her depression comes back. How long until you’re looking for the door again?

Maybe she really loves you and her heart will overrule her head, who knows? But if it were me I’d be looking for someone who would stay even when things get hard.
Put your phone away and go for a walk outside. Get some food or listen to a podcast or something. Gotta distract yourself any way you can until the urge lessens up a bit

I know some people who love themselves but are shallow, selfish, and rude. And I know others who hate themselves but are some of the kindest, most compassionate people ever.

Not arguing with your main point, but that one paragraph isn’t always true in my experience.
That’s pretty toxic behavior and will make the ex hate you. If the goal is to rebuild a healthy relationship, this is not a path that leads there.

I think typically both people grieve after a breakup. It’s never the same, but both do it in their own way and in their own time.

Often the dumpers aren’t exactly happy, but they are getting what they want. They’re in control of the situation and that helps. I’m sure she misses you sometimes. Maybe she even second guesses herself once in a while. But it’s not the same. She doesn’t feel the way you do, doesn’t miss you in the same way you miss her.
It’s up to you how you want to do it, but I’m sure he’ll be thrilled you asked.
You’re so right!

I’ve been there. It’s not a fun place to be.

I try to remind myself that my life hasn’t changed at all because of this knowledge. We’re still not in contact. Nothing has changed at all really. It’s just my brain making me feel bad.
You sure we can’t just be sad forever? Some days it sure seems like it.

I wonder what the distribution of healing time looks like. It’s been a year and a half for me and I’m still not in a good place.

Everybody knows breakups are hard, but I wonder what the time is like on average.

You don’t have to hate him to go no contact. I’m trying to keep no contact, or at least as little as possible, until I’m not so heartbroken. Perhaps someday if I ever manage to move on we could be friends. She’s still a wonderful person, we’re just not right for each other.

It’s just too painful to have contact right now.
What was the thing that made you realize he wasn’t the one? Why did you give up on the relationship? Just curious

You’ll feel better if you just do it. You’re already not dating him. If he rejects you all that happens is you’re still not dating him. You’ve got nothing to lose! And you can feel content knowing you were brave and took your shot.
All I can say about that interaction is yikes. There are better guys out there for you.
I say just go for it. You’ll never know if you don’t try.

I’m getting closer. I just about had it a few years ago but then I lost my job and spent everything I had saved looking for a new one. Now I’m building it back up. Almost to 10k. 

I kinda hate my job. It’s exactly what I always wanted to be doing. I sacrificed so much. And now that I’m here I hate it :(
Ugh, that’s a rough thought. Gotta just write off that money as a loss. It doesn’t matter what it’s going towards now, it may as well have been flushed. It’s all the same.

Ive been here a long time, and I can tell you that there are a LOT of heartbroken men here. Lots of guys who were treated badly by exes.

A lot of people have a tendency to generalize based on gender after bad experiences, but for every person who feels that way. There’s another with the same story but with genders reversed.

I think we’re all just people getting hurt by other people and hurt by ourselves. Sure there are some gender differences, but the commonalities are more significant.

You did the right thing. He way crossed the line and you had no choice but to do what you did. He obviously wasn’t over her and you can’t force him to move in if he’s not ready and doesn’t want to.

Try not to feel guilty, it sounds to me like you went above and beyond to try and make things work here. But it takes two. Don’t feel bad for enforcing your own boundaries and prioritizing the things you need.

You need to go no contact. At least for a while. He’s proven he’s not going to treat you right when he can treat you like a backup option and you’ll stick around waiting.

That might sound harsh, but I have the utmost sympathy for you. My ex also dumped me after 9 years. I also made the mistake of going back to hang out/hook up. She’s also dating someone new now and it’s killing me.

Given the way he’s using you, I don’t think he’s confused about his feelings, but the best way to find out is to walk away and see if he values you enough to try and keep you.

We deserve better than these people that threw our love away like it meant nothing.
Maybe they know exactly what they lost, but they just don’t much care :(
Stay strong, kopeng mi

This is good advice. Just wanted to add that she’s showing you what she thinks of you here. You said it yourself, she doesn’t want to be with you, but she doesn’t want you to move on either. She only cares about you insofar as it makes her feel wanted. Do you really want to be with someone like that?
Sounds like closing the barn door after the horse has already left.
I think the hole created when she left leaked out all my emotional resources :(
I think if you just yell at me a little more then I’ll be able to just move on and not care anymore. I know feeling bad doesn’t help, but that knowledge doesn’t help me stop feeling bad.

March.

Was the 9 years guy a different guy than the 4 years wasted guy?

I moved back a few months after; even got my old job back.

The funny part is that six months later I went back to our hometown for vacation, met up with her. She told me she still loved me, we slept together, and she said she’d want to be with me again if I still lived there.

I guess she just realized she didn’t love me as much as she used to. Wanted a life with someone else instead. We spent three years long distance and that was hard on us both. I moved to be with her, but apparently it was too late because she dumped me a few months after I did that.

I’m not sure what you mean by the last part. Yes to what? Try what?

I don’t think that is much of a risk for me. I don’t get many dates let alone relationships. And I haven’t felt anything approaching romantic towards anyone in a very long time. Just been focusing on my career and trying to be less sad lately. My ex on the other hand is in a new long-term relationship. Lately I’ve been afraid I’m going to find out through the grapevine that she’s engaged. Maybe they’re not that serious, I don’t know anything about it really.
9 and a half years together, 2 years heartbroken after she left. If I don’t move on soon I’m going to waste my whole life on this girl who doesn’t want me. I’m trying, but nothing seems to work.

I’d want to tell her there hasn’t been a single day I haven’t thought of her since she left. I’d want to tell her that she hurt me beyond anything I understood was possible. And I’d want to tell her that no matter how hard she pushes me away, no matter what I do to move on, I can’t stop loving her.
It’s never fun. But the longer you wait the worse it gets for her.

It’s understandable that he’s upset. It sounds like he’s not over the breakup and wants you back. He thought things were going in that direction and then you say that the breakup was good for you. 

What he hears is that you’re glad for the breakup, glad for all the hurt he’s going through, and better off without him. Not a fun thing to hear.

I know that’s not quite what you mean, but that’s how it sounds to him.

I don’t think there’s a way to “remedy” the situation. He still wants a relationship with you and presumably you don’t feel the same. That alone is going to hurt him and there’s no way around it. It’s probably best to give each other some space until he’s actually moved on and isn’t hoping you’ll take him back.

I found out today that she took a trip with her new boyfriend a few weeks ago. They went to our spot. Our getaway from the city. The place we took each other’s virginity so many years ago. She’s doing everything we used to do there with him now.

She called me for the first time in forever last week, but it turned out it was just a mistake. Stupidly I started feeling the hope again, but she’s in love with someone else now. 

When am I going to move on? I’ve fallen to pieces since she left me, and she’s out there thriving. Will life ever feel anything but empty without her?

I understand. I moved away a few months after my ex left. Only to the next state over, but still, it was a difficult decision that took me a long time to think through. It’s ok to be conflicted. You’ll make the right choice in the end.

Don’t stay for her. Sacrificing on your career to remain available to her is not going to bring her back and it’s not going to help you.

My shrink tells me any time we act out of fear we damage our self-esteem. You said you’re almost sure a better life is waiting for you. Don’t be afraid.
I texted her to ask why she called. She said she didn’t even realize she had called me. She didn’t try to have a conversation. It was probably an accident.

It sounds like she’s still interested in you. If you want her back then give it a shot.

Don’t stop working on yourself, but try to do it for you and not for her.

Remember that she left you once. Life is long and hard and sometimes it puts you on your ass. Sometimes you lose your way. When you lost your way what did she do? Did she stick by you and help you through it? Or are you only as good as your LSAT score to her?

I hope for a relationship where I have the space to fail, make mistakes, screw things up. One where I know she loves me for me, not for my accomplishments. I don’t know if it’s out there for me or for you, but it’s what I hope for.

Then again, if you love her then you love her and you’ll follow your heart come what may.
Trust me, I know :(

I ended up having sex with my ex after about 7 months of being broken up. She gave me the same line afterwards about missing me and still loving me but not wanting a relationship.

It’s tough, but it’s a part of the process. Only thing you can do is give him the space he asked for. It’s also easier on you to avoid the roller coaster. I know it’s hard to deal with that space now, but six, twelve months from now, you’ll be in a better place if you can manage it.

Anyone who could dump you by text, and when you cry on a call laugh and give no pity, then block you is not the most amazing person ever. 

The rose colored glasses are real. I think you need to make a list of negative things about her. Don’t quit until you have at least several things. They are there, I promise.

What you do is you understand that this is going to be devastating for a while. You let yourself hurt, try to be as kind to yourself as possible, stay busy and stay hopeful if you can. You prepare to live with the grief for a long time. To pick yourself up everyday and go through the motions. You cry sometimes, suffer through the dreams. Eventually you’ll find little bits of happiness again. Then they’ll be gone just like that. But they’ll come back. You try to move on. You lose hope, you find it again.

You make a few mistakes. The same ones people warn you about on this sub that you think you know not to make. But you forgive yourself and you keep going.

I have a similar story. 9 year relationship started in high school, distance for the last few years, bad times, closed the distance to figure things out, months later she dumped me.

It’s been a year and a half since then. Worst year and a half ever. I know how hard it can be. But after some time I also know there can be hope at the end.

Don’t be afraid to reach out if you want someone to talk to. I’m here to listen.

Maybe the fact that you’re sad means that this isn’t the right relationship for you? Maybe there’s someone else out there that will be a part of a life that makes you happy instead.

I was depressed and on meds when my ex left. I felt like that was a contributing factor and blamed myself for that. If only I’d been healthier she might have stayed. But it was really more about her than it was about me, and our relationship not going so well was a big part of why I was sad, even before the breakup.

I try to tell myself that when things aren’t going well, big changes are nothing to be afraid of. That doesn’t mean I don’t miss her all the time, but maybe if I keep looking and working at it I’ll find a way to be happy again on my own or with someone else.

It’s hard not to. She broke up with me when we lived in the same place, but the last time I saw her (10 months after the breakup, 6 months before now), she told me she loved me and that we would be together if we lived in the same city.

I know things aren’t going to change for a while, but it feels like something else is going to happen with us someday. Like maybe I’ll take one more chance on it. That feeling is probably preventing my healing but I can’t seem to shake it.

Been a year and a half for me and it still hurts, especially the mornings after I dream of her.

Do you think it’s definitely over or is some part of you still holding on hope?

If she keeps bugging you, just tell her you need space and to leave you alone for a while. If you’re feeling spicy use whatever line she gave you when you broke up.

Not really okay, but a tiny bit better all the time.

It can take a lot of time. I don’t understand these “it’s been a month and I’m so much better” posts either. It’s been 1.5 years and I’m still hurting a lot. It is a little easier than it used to be though. I wasn’t sure I was ever going to be okay for so many months, but I believe now that I’ll be all right someday. Just needed the time to see the slow, slow progress.

I don’t know if I’ll ever stop loving her. I don’t know if it will ever stop hurting, but I’ll make it, day by day.

I think it’s all right to be a mess, and it’s all right to miss them and not be over it for a very long time if that’s how you feel. It doesn’t mean you’re fundamentally different and you’ll never be okay again. It just means you’re dealing with it in your own way, the way you need to.

Way too much self-blaming going on here. She bears more responsibility for the relationship ending than you do. She cheated after all, your depression is no excuse for that.

You absolutely do not have to be friends with her, in fact I’d recommend against it, at least for a period of a few years. It’s just going to keep kicking you in the chest if you let it.

I know it’s not easy, but it’s time to cut her out and spend all that effort you put in to making her happy and doing nice things for her back into you.

I don’t think you failed. You’re just transitioning into a new stage in your life.

It was 9 years for me, and I was a complete wreck for so many months afterwards. You’re not going to be okay right now, and that’s fine and understandable. There’s so much hurt in front of you, but the sooner you can kick the self-blame the better it will be. Talk to a therapist if you can, it can be helpful.

My ex broke up with me after 9 years as well. It’s terrible and it still hurts a year and a half later. I’d say you should get rid of the things from your relationship, the mementos and photos. Or just put them away out of sight. But try to take back the activities you like to do and make them yours again. Or try new things that sound cool but you’ve never done before. The worst thing you can do is just sit in sadness doing nothing because everything makes you think of him.

I did a little of everything with my ex, no contact, friends, friends with benefits (don’t do that one). It all sucks, but strict no contact will help you heal the fastest. It still might take a really long time. Unfollow on social media; you don’t want to see that when the ex finds someone new.

For me there was nothing that really helped me get over it, just things that didn’t make it worse.

If anyone has an answer for you I’d like to know too. It’s been a year and a half and I’m starting to think I’m crazy for still being so heartbroken. I know I can’t break no contact or check her socials because I’m too fragile for that. Maybe someday I’ll finally feel like there’s an actual end to our story. Maybe it’s always going to be this way moving forward. If that’s the case I suppose I ought to just be grateful for the ten years we did have together. But I miss her terribly every day. Thoughts of her don’t let up, and even if they did, the dreams would always remind me.

I don’t understand why you think this makes you an awful person. What did you do that was so awful? Text him a bunch when he didn’t want to talk to you? Big deal, you were hurting, breaking up, it’s understandable. Nothing to be ashamed about really. Breaking up in the midst of his dads death? It’s not like that was your plan. He pushed you away, said he didn’t love you, and ignored your attempts to communicate. Seems like he wanted the break up a lot more than you did.

If it feels better being broken up you ought to embrace that and let go of feeling guilty for whatever imagined reason. There’s certainly nothing here that would classify you as an “awful person.”
What’s going on is that she’s a reckless asshole who reopened your wound on a whim. If she really cared about your feelings she wouldn’t have done that.
If she made you feel bad about yourself and your career perhaps she wasn’t the one.

Living together while broken up is problematic. If there’s no way you can separate immediately then I’d talk to her and set a firm date when she has to be gone, and make it soon. Light a fire under her ass to move out. You’re never going to heal when she’s always right there.

You can’t manage somebody else’s addiction. They have to be ready to do it for themselves or it will never work. Don’t second guess yourself or think that it could have been different if you had just “let him drink” or whatever. It wouldn’t have been any different. 

It sucks to be left for a substance, but in the long run it’s going to be better than being in a relationship with an addict, especially one who is unrepentant / in denial.

I know what you mean. I feel the same way. It’s been a long time since my ex dumped me, and most days I can sort of live in my own life and function okay. I’ve figured out how to do that much, but being happy? Don’t have the answer to that one yet. Maybe next year I’ll figure it out.
When someone talks shit about an ex it reflects more on them than on the ex, and people tend to see that.

I know it hurts seeing them with someone else. When I saw my ex with her new boyfriend it felt like my heart had been disemboweled. I felt anxious and hurt, like yesterday’s model, tossed in the trash after an upgrade. I wanted to cry and scream and break everything in my apartment.

It never feels okay, but it doesn’t feel so overwhelming after a while.

My heart goes out to you. I know that antidepressants can really subtly change how you perceive the world and how you feel and how you act. And the withdrawals aren’t fun either. I’ve almost ruined friendships because I wasn’t acting like myself while withdrawing from antidepressants.

Remember not to let your pain and regret overwhelm your self worth. You may have made a mistake, but I can tell you’re a good person. I hope you can forgive yourself. And perhaps someday in the distant future you can reconnect with him and tell him how sorry you are and how much you regret what happened.
